Where a segmentation puts its boundaries, sentence by sentence

Source: R/doc-segment-quality.R
gr_seg_boundaries.Rd

Turns a segmentation into the boundary sequence gr_seg_pk() and gr_seg_windowdiff() compare: the document is split into sentences, each sentence is placed in a segment, and position j is 1 when sentence j + 1 is in a later segment than sentence j. Two segmentations of one document mapped this way are on the same units and can be compared.

Usage

gr_seg_boundaries(x, doc)

Arguments

x

A gr_chunks from gr_segment(), or a character vector of segments in document order (a reference segmentation, for example the document's topics as a person split them).

doc

The document x segments: a gr_document from gr_ingest(), or text.

Value

An integer vector of 0 and 1 with one element per pair of neighbouring sentences (the number of sentences less one), with attributes units (the number of sentences) and unplaced.

Details

A segment is matched on its text with runs of white space made one space, and on a chunk's source_text when it has one, so the context line of a contextual chunk is not part of the match. When every segment is a verbatim part of the document, each segment and each sentence is located in the document, in order, and a sentence goes to the first segment that holds its first character. A sentence the document repeats, such as "See note 3." at the start of two sections, therefore goes to the segment it occurs in, not to the first segment whose text contains it. A boundary inside a sentence counts at the end of that sentence, and overlap does not add boundaries: a sentence carried into the next chunk stays in the first chunk that holds its start.

When a segment is not verbatim (a segmenter that rewrites text, or a reference typed by hand), sentences are matched on text instead: each in the current segment after the text the sentences before it took, or in a later segment; failing that, by its opening, its first 40 characters or its first half when that is shorter. A sentence placed neither way stays in the segment before it and is counted in the unplaced attribute.

See also

gr_seg_pk(), gr_seg_windowdiff(), gr_seg_recall()

Other segmentation functions: gr_check_segmenter(), gr_chunk_stats(), gr_chunks, gr_register_segmenter(), gr_seg_pk(), gr_seg_recall(), gr_segment(), gr_segment_spec(), gr_segmenters(), new_chunks()

Examples

doc <- paste("Revenue rose. Costs fell.", "Staff grew. Offices moved.",
             "The chair retired.", sep = "\n\n")
gr_seg_boundaries(c("Revenue rose. Costs fell.", "Staff grew. Offices moved.",
                    "The chair retired."), doc)
#> [1] 0 1 0 1
#> attr(,"units")
#> [1] 5
#> attr(,"unplaced")
#> [1] 0
ch <- gr_segment(doc, list(method = "sentence", max_tokens = 32))
#> Ingested 3 block(s), ~26 tokens (0 chars removed by cleaning).
#> Segmenting with 'sentence' (cap 32 tokens, overlap 0).
gr_seg_boundaries(ch, doc)
#> [1] 0 0 0 1
#> attr(,"units")
#> [1] 5
#> attr(,"unplaced")
#> [1] 0
